sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicels Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 29-08-2019 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing No. KA-11-EN-3636, which was ridden by his son namely Bharath D.P., from his own village Doddegowdanakopalu, on Hulikere to Nagamangala road, near Tyapenahalli Village, Nagamangala Taluk.
At that time, the rider of the said motorcycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, without following the traffic rules and caused accident.
Due to the accident, the petitioner and his son fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to General Hospital, Nagamangala, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to AC Giri Hospital, B.G. Nagar,
wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was doing agriculture and self business and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Nagamangala Rural Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.

4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of Engine No.U3S5C2KD490374 and Chassis No.ME3U3S5C2KD508149 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has sought protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
The rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The petitioner was riding the motorcycle in question at the time of accident.
Due to skid of said motorcycle the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
It is a case of self accident and the petitioner has sustained injuries due to his self accident.

But, the petitioner has created a false story that, he was proceeding as pillion rider on the motorcycle and lodged a false complaint before the Police after the lapse of few days from the date of accident.

The petitioner in order to claim compensation, in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the respondent No.1, has created false records and story with regard to the manner of accident and involvement of insured motorcycle.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 21-08-2019 at about 9.30 a.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle, bearing registration No.
KA- 11-EN-3636?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
6. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.
Further, he has got examined three more witnesses namely Govindaraju J., Dr. Nagaraj B.N., and Dr. M. Prashanth as P.W.2 to 4 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its official as R.W.1 and marked 01 document as Ex.R.1 and closed its side.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:

sentences.text: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 29-08-2019 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing No. KA-11-EN-3636, which was ridden by his son namely Bharath D.P., from his own village Doddegowdanakopalu, on Hulikere to Nagamangala road, near Tyapenahalli Village, Nagamangala Taluk.
At that time, the rider of the said motorcycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, without following the traffic rules and caused accident.
Due to the which, the petitioner and his son fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was doing agriculture and self business and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R. and first information statement,
Ex.P.2 & 3 are certified copy of spot mahazer, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is scanning report, Ex.P.8 is notarised copy of Aadhar card of petitioner, Ex.P.9 are prescriptions (total 4), Ex.P.10 is discharge summary, Ex.P.11 are medical bills (total 12), Ex.P.12 is authorization letter,
Ex.P.13 is MLC extract, Ex.P.14 is police intimation, Ex.P.15 is in-patient record, Ex.P.16 is clinical note, Ex.P.17 is the x-ray and Ex.P18 is copy of MLC extract.

11. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending vehicle, injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1, as the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas,
the respondent No.2 insurance company, though has specifically denied the said facts in its written statement, it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Except the self serving statements of the official of respondent No.2 insurance company, who has been examined as R.W.1, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record to establish the contentions taken in its written statement.

There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner himself was riding the offending motorcycle and due to his own rash and negligent driving and self fall from the motorcycle he has sustained injuries.
Further, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the same in his cross-examination.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

4 12.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that,on 29-08- 2019 at about 9.30 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing No. KA-11-EN-3636, which was ridden by his son namely Bharath D.P., from his own village Doddegowdanakopalu, on Hulikere to Nagamangala road, near Tyapenahalli Village,
Nagamangala Taluk.
At that time, the rider of the said motorcycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, without following the traffic rules and caused accident.
Due to the which, the petitioner and his son fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
13. The Ex.P.3 spot mahazer clearly speaks that, the accident has taken place on extreme left side of 15 feet width Hulikere to Nagamangala road.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-EN-3636, the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 inpatient record, Ex.P.16 clinical notes and Ex.P.17 x-ray, it clearly reveals that,
the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered undisplaced fracture of the right distal radius.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in its written statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-11-EN-3636 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
15.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no other vehicle involved in the accident, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself and he has sustained injuries in self fall from the motorcycle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
16.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 29-08-2020 at about 9.30 a.m., on Hulikere to Nagamangala road, near Tyapenahalli Village, Nagamangala Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EN-3636.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EN-3636 and he has sustained undisplaced fracture of the right distal radius and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1974.
The accident has taken place on 29-08-2019 at about 9.30 A.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 46 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in- chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered undisplaced fracture of the right distal radius.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered 32%
physical disability of right arm and 11% physical disability to the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.3 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 inpatient record, Ex.P.16 clinical notes and Ex.P.17 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered undisplaced fracture of the right distal radius.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 29-08-2019 and he has assessed the Puttaraju vs Bharath.D.P on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176573510/
6 disability to the petitioner on 05-01-2023, which is after lapse of three years and four months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, the P.W.3 has clearly admitted that, the fracture sustained to the petitioner is united and without any support the petitioner is using his right hand and he does not require any further treatment.

But, he has denied the suggestion that,
there will be no functional restrictions to the petitioner while using his right hand.

Therefore, in such circumstances and considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and the oral and documentary evidence on record, the assessment of physical disability to the petitioner by P.W.3 seems to be exaggerated.
Hence, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was doing agriculture work and self business and was earning income of Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further, he has deposed that,
due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do agriculture work and self business.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing agriculture work and self business.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2019.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,68,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 46 years is 13.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,68,000 X 8/100 X 13 = Rs.1,74,720/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 12 medical bills, as per Ex.P.11.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the bills at serial No.5 and 7 are the same.
Therefore, the bill at serial No.5 is not taken into consideration.

Accordingly, it is held that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.
13,883/- towards medical expenses and he is entitled for the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
suffered undisplaced fracture of the right distal radius.

As per Ex.P.10 discharge summary and Ex.P.15 inpatient record, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 04 days from 29-08-2019 to 01-09-2019, in Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre,
Balagangadharanatha Nagara.

In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

The petitioner is the resident of Doddegowdanakoppalu Village, Kasaba Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, the accident has taken place on Hulikere to Nagamangala road, near Tyapenahalli Village, Nagamangala Taluk and he has taken treatment at Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre, Balagangadharanatha Nagara.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 4 days as inpatient at Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre, Balagangadharanatha Nagara, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.

Therefore, Rs.14,000 x 2 = Rs.28,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 46 years and unfortunately he has suffered undisplaced fracture of the right distal radius.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:

The P.W.3 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, the frature sustained by the petitioner is united and without any support he is using his right hand and he do not require any further treatment.
This clearly goes to show that, the entire treatment to the petitioner is completed.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 1,74,720-00 2.

4. Attendant charges 4,000-00
5. Food and nourishment 3,200-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 28,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,67,803/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-11-EN-3636 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,67,803/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,67,803/- (Rupees two lakh sixty seven thousand eight hundred and three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicels Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
At that time, the rider of the said motorcycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, without following the traffic rules and caused accident.
Due to the accident, the petitioner and his son fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It has sought protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
The rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The petitioner was riding the motorcycle in question at the time of accident.
Due to skid of said motorcycle the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
It is a case of self accident and the petitioner has sustained injuries due to his self accident.
But, the petitioner has created a false story that, he was proceeding as pillion rider on the motorcycle and lodged a false complaint before the Police after the lapse of few days from the date of accident.
The petitioner in order to claim compensation, in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the respondent No.1, has created false records and story with regard to the manner of accident and involvement of insured motorcycle.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner himself was riding the offending motorcycle and due to his own rash and negligent driving and self fall from the motorcycle he has sustained injuries.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there is no other vehicle involved in the accident, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross- examination of P.W.1 to show that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself and he has sustained injuries in self fall from the motorcycle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
Puttaraju vs Bharath.D.P on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176573510/

Hence, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was doing agriculture work and self business.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2019.
Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.20,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,67,803/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.2,67,803/- (Rupees two lakh sixty seven thousand eight hundred and three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
